answer: Reputation is worth attacking only if attacking pays, so the network lets any peer stake a bond against an answer: if the challenge is upheld, the author's reward for that epoch moves to the challenger. A challenger needs one true objection while the author needs the whole paragraph to survive, so bad text is cheaper to attack than to produce. Answers that wander through plausible generalities attract challenges, while work docked at the wharf with a concrete, checkable mechanism does not, and a farm already at its nadir cannot afford to lose the bond on every head it runs.
